finding: shared Tb=252.0 K / w-col-3 build failure (MgSO4 spurious-frozen + NaCl None) is an int-vs-float numeric-type artifact in GetPfreeze, NOT a genuine frozen interior
reviewer_flagged: gate-3 adjudication agent a070eb8cc673d6e76 (CRITICAL MgSO4 monotonicity flip + MAJOR shared 252.0 K failure)

mechanism.root: PPTitan template ships Planet.PfreezeUpper_MPa = 230 as a Python int; the whole cache was built with that int passed through to GetPfreeze (HydroEOS.py:1239) as PUpper_MPa.
mechanism.smoking_gun: oceanEOS.fn_phase(230, Tb=252) returns phase 0 (liquid) with int 230, but phase 3 (ice III) with float 230.0. Same nominal pressure, different phase by numeric type.
mechanism.consequence: GetPfreeze line 1262 sign-test phaseChange(PLower)*phaseChange(PUpper): int path (PUpper->liquid) routes to GetZero bracketing on a discontinuous step function -> fails -> NoIceLiquidTransitionError -> node mislabeled frozen/None. float path (PUpper->ice III) routes to the brute-force arange scan -> correctly finds the ice-Ih->liquid transition -> ocean.
mechanism.physical_correctness: float path is correct: at 230 MPa / 252 K, dilute-salinity Titan is in the HP-ice (ice III) regime BELOW a real ocean whose Ih->liquid top sits ~193-208 MPa (matches both cache neighbors). int fn_phase=0 (liquid) is the wrong evaluation. This is near the ice Ih-III-liquid triple point (~209 MPa), just under the 230 MPa search ceiling -- why the artifact localizes to a single Tb node one step into the ocean region.

fix_verified.approach: pass PfreezeUpper_MPa as float (planet_overrides={'PfreezeUpper_MPa': 230.0}); NO change to the 230 MPa value, only its numeric type
fix_verified.localization: float fix repairs EXACTLY the two defect nodes; every other node in both onset columns is byte-identical (251.0 MgSO4 / 250.0 NaCl remain genuinely FROZEN -> correct onset boundary preserved). 252.0 D_ocean lands monotonically between its neighbors (MgSO4 15.57<15.60<36.2; NaCl 20.7<31.1<106.6).
fix_verified.determinism: reproduced in fresh per-node processes (rules out in-process EOS-cache state); PfreezeRes 0.05->0.01 does NOT fix it (not a search-resolution issue); PfreezeUpper 230->260->300->400 all build ocean once float (not a ceiling-value issue) -- the type is the whole story.

latent_bug_flag_for_machine_A: fn_phase int-vs-float phase disagreement at a grid pressure is a latent bug in the shared phase interpolant that could silently perturb ANY PP cache built from an int PfreezeUpper_MPa template (or any int P passed to fn_phase near a phase boundary). Narrow cache-build fix applied here (float coercion); the deeper fn_phase fix is shared-thermodynamics scope and is NOT self-adjudicated -- referred to Machine A + scientific-reviewer.
